intro: In the Northern Mariana Islands, the past sits out in the weather. It is carved into limestone latte pillars, rested along island reefs, and carried through generations of conversation across Saipan, Tinian, and Rota.
House of Taga is a reporter’s notebook written off deadline. It is a space for the stories that warrant a second, deeper look after the daily news cycle moves on.

find.title: Ancient Ground & Heritage
find.text: Notes on archaeology, ancient navigation, and the early history of Chamorro and Refaluwasch culture.

find.title: Colonial Layers & Memory
find.text: Stories, archival records, and figures from the Spanish, German, and Japanese eras.

find.title: Footprints of War
find.text: The lingering human and physical impact of World War II across the archipelago.

find.title: Island Dispatches
find.text: Essays, background context, and observations on local life and civic history in the CNMI.

closing: My goal here is simple: to document these island stories with care, keep a clear record of what took place, and preserve details that might otherwise slip away.
